README.md:188:Phase 1 implementation began on 2026-06-10 with the multi-repo scaffold under the `UbU-project` organization: `ubu-schemas`, `ubu-core`, `ubu-store`, `ubu-github-adapter`, `ubu-planning-kernel`, `ubu-orchestrator`, `ubu-ui`, `ubu-devshell`, and `ubu-brand`, initialized in bootstrap-dependency order with rev-pinned cross-repo dependencies and per-repo CI. Cross-repo authority boundaries are canonical in `docs/PHASE1_CONTRACT_BOUNDARIES.md`. The scaffold is a complete walking skeleton of the architecture; Phase 1 feature semantics are implemented incrementally against the frozen design in the priority order of `DESIGN.md` §4.1.6. The scaffold-reconciliation decisions `UBU-D0226` through `UBU-D0230` and the store-wiring decision `UBU-D0231` landed first, then the first user-facing slice (`UBU-D0232`): a bootstrap interview seeds Objectives, Preferences, and Tasks through admission, and a deterministic readiness-ordered next-action recommendation with act and override drives a one-next-Task loop. On that base, GitHub projection landed: preview → per-batch approval → worker write → reconciliation with conflict surfacing, restricted to managed labels and implementing `UBU-D0159` (`UBU-D0233`); and the export boundary was made real — a single authoritative Legitimizer issues a deny-by-default export permit, the orchestrator can reach no external write without it, and worker-authority and redaction-identity export-boundary invariants are enforced with standing hard-boundary checks (`UBU-D0234`, extending `UBU-D0230`). Phase A of the planning slice then landed (`UBU-D0235`): a canonical timed Plan, deterministic skeleton Compact Calendar generation, override-safe recalculation, and a fixed-seed golden-fixture corpus. Phase B added affect legitimization (`UBU-D0236`): the planning kernel's `full_legitimize` now applies the §6 sigmoid affect filter — per-dimension satisfaction against a separate AffectProfile and the snapshot observation, with `enforce` and `warn_only` modes — and `next_action` is sourced from the affect-legitimized Calendar. The `ubu-devshell` fixture smoke test exercises the full onboard-to-act loop, the gated projection loop including the deny path, and the affect-legitimized planning loop, offline against a mock GitHub backend. Phase C-1 then added the optimization layer (`UBU-D0237`): the kernel generates a bounded candidate set (the legitimized skeleton baseline plus deterministic slack-based perturbations, capped at sixteen), runs the affect filter per candidate, prunes with semi-legitimization (`UBU-D0211`), and value-scores survivors into a `scoring_policy`-weighted composite `total_score` with role-tagged alternatives; the default Calendar is the rank-1 candidate and `next_action` follows it. The same decision made the kernel contract types the planning surface and removed the stale thin `ubu-schemas` planning-request/response/task-spec stubs (C-1.5). The Monte Carlo rollout, probability estimation, live GitHub, and risk reports remain the next slices.

README.md:430:## `model-committee` bootstrap project
README.md:432:`model-committee` is the first runnable bootstrap automation project for active pre-MVP UbU dogfooding. It is an advisory Automation Worker pattern that reads canonical repo state, identifies answerable open questions, generates candidate changesets, scores those changesets, validates patches, and writes reviewable artifacts.
README.md:438:`model-committee` v0.3 implements the v0.2 frontier cross-scoring workflow and adds these important constraints:
README.md:440:- `PLANNING_KERNEL_CONTRACT.md` is the fourth model-committee input file, read by providers, injected into prompts, snapshotted in runs, and allowed in patches.
README.md:441:- `rank` may write `Answerability score:` and `Last scored:` back to `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`; it does not update `Scored from commit:`.
README.md:445:- Ollama remains a local work-proposal provider and does not score in v0.3.
README.md:448:`model-committee` must remain bounded. It must not implement direct OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or GitHub API calls; auto-merge; auto-push; automatic pull request creation; automatic artifact publication; automatic patch application; adaptive model weights; multi-turn Claude Code sessions; full Association automation; or UbU planning-kernel work.
README.md:454:`model-committee` uses answerability as the first gate. A question is eligible for ordinary work only if it has no dependencies, all dependencies are solved, or all dependencies are being answered in the same work item.

DESIGN.md:606:### 3.1.1 v0.2 Claude Code and cross-scoring provider model
DESIGN.md:608:`model-committee v0.2` adds Claude Code CLI as a second frontier provider for both work proposal generation and scoring.
DESIGN.md:610:The v0.2 provider model is not raw majority voting. It is cross-scored adversarial review:

DESIGN.md:626:v0.2 automated selection requires at least one valid work proposal, at least one valid cross-score from a different frontier provider, no hard validation failure on the selected patch, and no critical disagreement flag unless manually overridden outside automatic selection. DESIGN.md:684:The accepted work-phase contract is intentionally mechanical. A work proposal is a schema-validated envelope containing provider identity, model name, selected question or problem ID, base commit, summary, rationale, changed-file list, a raw unified diff, suggested commit message, validation notes, declared new questions, declared resolved questions, declared decisions, and a human-review flag. The patch is the authoritative changeset; prose summaries are explanatory only.
DESIGN.md:686:Before scoring, `model-committee` validates the proposal envelope, base commit, allowed file set, referenced question and decision IDs, patch syntax, patch applicability against the recorded base snapshot, and any work-item-specific semantic checks. For current design-document work, the v0.1 writable set is limited to `DESIGN.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, and `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`. Later code, schema, fixture, and bug-fix work generalizes by declaring an allowed path set plus validators, tests, and artifact expectations for the selected work item.
DESIGN.md:688:Only mechanically valid proposals are eligible for automatic selection. Invalid proposals are retained in logs with diagnostics, but they are not quorum evidence. If a selected proposal later fails patch validation, automatic selection fails rather than silently applying a different patch; the run writes review artifacts and uses the invalid-selected-patch failure path.
DESIGN.md:690:Work scoring considers at least correctness against the selected question or problem, consistency with accepted decisions, mechanical validity, minimality, reviewability, risk and reversibility, validation or test adequacy, maintainability, and whether the changeset preserves model-committee authority boundaries. Score records must name required fixes and validation assumptions. Self-scores may be retained as diagnostics, but only non-self scores count for quorum evidence. v0.1 uses Codex scoring over valid Codex and Ollama proposals; v0.2 requires frontier cross-scoring between Codex and Claude Code as described above.
DESIGN.md:692:`model-committee` v0.1 and v0.2 do not automatically apply patches, commit locally, push artifacts, open pull requests, or mutate GitHub. A human operator may apply `selected.patch`, inspect `review.md`, rerun appropriate checks, and create a normal local commit using `commit_message.txt` as a suggestion. Any future automatic local commit path requires a later accepted decision with explicit clean-worktree, validation, and approval rules.
DESIGN.md:696:Model-committee runs use a prioritized recursive loop:
DESIGN.md:700:3. **Work** produces and scores concrete changesets.
DESIGN.md:702:Each run should record loop state in its manifest or review artifact: base commit, canonical input hashes, consistency status, blocking failure IDs, warning IDs, selected loop mode, selected work item, provider/version baseline, and whether any derived scores were reused or invalidated.
DESIGN.md:709:- prompt, schema, validator, quorum, provider-weight, provider-config, or model-committee tool-version changes;
DESIGN.md:715:Hard consistency failures block ordinary prioritization and ordinary work. Hard failures include missing or unparseable canonical files, duplicate question or decision IDs, malformed question metadata, dependency references to missing questions, dependency cycles, invalid `Resolved by` references, solved/decomposed/deferred/superseded status contradictions, selected-work dependency violations, patch-base mismatch, forbidden-path proposals, and canonical input changes after the recorded consistency snapshot.
DESIGN.md:717:Warnings do not block prioritization when they cannot invalidate the selected work item. Warnings include stale derived documents, unscored or `TBD` ranking fields, optional provider failures when quorum remains satisfiable, nonblocking provider version drift, stale historical scores, and derived artifact publication gaps. Prioritization may run with warnings only when the warning list is recorded and stale scores are excluded from automatic selection.
DESIGN.md:719:When hard failures exist, the next selectable work is consistency repair, decomposition, or diagnostic work for those failures. A consistency failure should be converted into a problem record with stable failure key, severity, affected files or object IDs, evidence, suggested repair, and whether a human decision is required. If the repair is mechanical and inside the current allowed file set, model-committee may solicit repair patches. If the repair exposes an unresolved design choice, it may create or update an open question; new MVP blockers must satisfy the `UBU-D0175` blocker-certificate rule.
DESIGN.md:723:LLM model updates and provider CLI updates do not retroactively change committed canonical design state or historical run logs. ## `model-committee` bootstrap project

`model-committee` is the first runnable bootstrap automation project for active pre-MVP UbU dogfooding. It is an advisory Automation Worker pattern that reads canonical repo state, identifies answerable open questions, generates candidate changesets, scores those changesets, validates patches, and writes reviewable artifacts.

Accepted design state exists only when committed to the canonical `ubu-design` repository.

### v0.3 boundary

`model-committee` v0.3 implements the v0.2 frontier cross-scoring workflow and adds these important constraints:

- `PLANNING_KERNEL_CONTRACT.md` is the fourth model-committee input file, read by providers, injected into prompts, snapshotted in runs, and allowed in patches.
- `rank` may write `Answerability score:` and `Last scored:` back to `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`; it does not update `Scored from commit:`.
- `work-generate` should prompt models to tombstone solved questions, remove duplicate information across source files, and compress content to the effective minimum.
- rendered prompt size at or above 90% of the configured warning limit must set `manifest.prompt_size_warning = true` and be surfaced in `review.md`.
- `manifest.schema_version` is `"0.3"`.
- Ollama remains a local work-proposal provider and does not score in v0.3.
- Fake provider mode remains deterministic and must not call Codex, Claude, or Ollama.

`model-committee` must remain bounded. It must not implement direct OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or GitHub API calls; auto-merge; auto-push; automatic pull request creation; automatic artifact publication; automatic patch application; adaptive model weights; multi-turn Claude Code sessions; full Association automation; or UbU planning-kernel work.

## Question selection and design-burden reduction

`model-committee` uses answerability as the first gate. A question is eligible for ordinary work only if it has no dependencies, all dependencies are solved, or all dependencies are being answered in the same work item.

Blocked questions may be selected for decomposition work if decomposition should produce replacement questions with fewer, simpler, or no dependencies. UbU should not treat every increase in open-question count as failure. The relevant metric is unresolved design burden, not raw question count.

Moves, cancellations and series changes supersede prior active reservations through ordinary admission while preserving logged history; absence from an incomplete response cannot establish cancellation.

Fixed busy commitments use capacity-occupying Static Tasks at validated UTC start/end times and bound chunks under `UBU-D0279`. Capture counts, Calendar display and Task existence alone do not prove occupancy. Verify the CPU reference path and each enabled planner backend against expected occupied/free intervals: flexible placements cannot enter busy time, and a source occurrence, its projection and its temporary blocker cannot consume capacity twice. Distinct commitments that genuinely overlap retain their conflict rather than being deduplicated by time.

Before removal, show the exact blocker replacements and residual intervals and obtain explicit operator approval bound to the manifest and current versions. Apply them through ordinary admission as one batch, or an equivalent serialized handoff that prevents Plan certification/projection of intermediate missing or doubled occupancy. Invalidate affected Plans and certify recalculation before reuse or projection. Failure or stale inputs preserve protection and require fresh review. Retire only the identified workaround, preserving source commitments and history. Advancing the horizon or receiving material source changes requires renewed coverage checks before using affected capacity; missing, stale or policy-withheld data never proves free time. Evidence and diagnostics obey current Compartment policy; this process neither grants capture/export authority nor bypasses existing sync/projection checks.

**Qualification phase (`UBU-D0384`).** The hardware, runtime, route and cost qualification below (`UBU-D0331`–`UBU-D0382` for `UBU-Q0177` and `UBU-Q0178`) is Phase 3 work: it closes on real-device evidence, not on further specification. Phase 2 builds the capture slices of §4.2 without enabling them.

**Measured local multimodal hardware (`UBU-D0331`).** Qualify an exact physical-hardware/software profile, separately identifying every execution-enclave Device and its capture, review, inference and optional planning roles. Pin hardware/RAM, OS build and security-update posture, drivers/runtime, model and weights digest, quantization, context/media sizes, storage/key configuration, UbU/template and policy revisions. Declare enabled sources, latency classes, concurrency, supported session duration and operating conditions. Primary mobile interaction does not select a full mobile planner or compute API (`UBU-Q0160`); capture-mode/device allocation and delivery sequence remain `UBU-Q0183`.

Before testing, freeze the scenario set, useful-outcome rubric and finite acceptance limits for quality, latency/freshness, memory/storage, battery/thermal behavior and cancellation. Use §21.1.3's ordinary interaction and text/form workflows, with synthetic or expressly consented fixtures covering visible details, exact names/values, noisy speech, ambiguity, corrections and unsupported requests. Review grounding, preserved uncertainty, fabricated assertions, correction burden and useful candidate-to-admission/next-action outcomes; transcripts, token rates and plausible conversation alone cannot pass. Count accepted, corrected, unresolved, rejected and failed outcomes separately over all trials. Numeric interaction profiles follow §21.1.4 and remain `UBU-Q0168`'s measured work.

For each proposed Device/backend/mode, run at least 30 cold-start and 100 warm trials using the pinned fixtures, plus at least 30 minutes of its proposed concurrent capture/inference/UI workload and the full maximum supported session if longer. Measure the complete capture-to-review route, including any authorized worker transfer. Record ambient conditions, charging/battery state, competing load, instrumentation and repeat procedure. Report §21.1.4's separate timings with sample counts, median, p95, maximum and misses/errors; include peak aggregate CPU/accelerator memory, model loading, buffers/caches and concurrent manual/planning work at the declared state/context limits. Report model/state/approved-artifact storage, peak scratch and required free-space reserve, energy/battery measurements and uncertainty, temperature/throttling and performance over time. Unavailable metrics stay explicit; missing evidence for a required limit prevents qualification. A short successful run cannot establish sustained or longer-session support.

Endpoint qualification must demonstrate a maintained security-update posture, installation/model integrity checks, OS access isolation, protected Device keys and access-controlled encrypted persistent storage with documented key custody and recovery. State the threat envelope: locked-device loss, unauthorized unprivileged processes, unintended persistence and unauthorized egress; do not claim protection from a compromised OS or malicious local administrator. Exercise source/Device revocation, lock/restart, denied reads/egress, storage exhaustion and interrupted cleanup. Inventory raw/intermediate/retained copies, OS/runtime swap, hibernation, crash dumps, caches and backups; enforce §12.2 and §21.1.5 on every applicable path or disable the affected mode. Encryption alone cannot satisfy transient-media retention. A rooted/debug planning-parity device supplies no endpoint-security evidence by itself; hardware attestation remains optional under DEVICE_SYNC_AND_COMPARTMENT_CONTRACT.md §26, and cleanup establishes no forensic-erasure guarantee.

Publish a policy-safe support matrix linking the exact profile, enabled workflows/classes, measured usable-memory/free-storage envelope, quality and timing results, sustained operating duration, security/retention outcomes and demonstrated fallback. Test offline/model loss, low battery, thermal/resource pressure, stop/silence, delayed results and manual completion without hidden cloud routing or loss of permitted saved state. A worker on another Device needs its own qualified endpoint/profile and existing route/Compartment checks; a same-Device worker remains an execution context unless separately admitted under §23.1. Ownership grants no disclosure authority. Only profiles passing all declared limits and mandatory security/retention gates may be operator-approved for those slices; material profile changes require affected rechecks. Label the selected configuration a tested sufficient profile among the tested candidates, with failures and limitations visible; infer no universal phone minimum or local-versus-cloud quality ranking. `UBU-Q0177` stays Open until a reviewed evidence-backed profile is selected; a protocol alone cannot close it. Lower-cost reach remains `UBU-Q0178`.

**Inference runtime reuse qualification (`UBU-D0336`).** Extend the endpoint gate to the deployed runtime's effective process permissions and source-dependent state across jobs. Inventory prompt/KV caches, embeddings, decoded media, buffers, leased handles and scratch separately from verified read-only model weights. A warm process or shared weights grant no access to prior job context. Enforce §21.1.5's lifecycle before reuse; separately authorized retained artifacts enter a new job only through fresh broker access and current bindings. If safe reuse cannot be demonstrated, qualify an isolated per-job runtime or leave the affected mode unavailable.

Run paired synthetic camera-and-voice jobs A/B under distinct grants, with B denied A's source and context. Put a unique synthetic detail in A and request it from B without supplying it. Exercise both job orders, ordinary completion, cancellation and source/policy revocation, crash/restart and resource pressure; include overlapping jobs only where concurrency is proposed. Inspect B's actual supplied context, runtime reads, result/artifact releases, cache/handle lookups and diagnostics for unauthorized A content or identifiers. Probe ambient filesystem, credential, camera/microphone and network access through the runtime's actual interfaces under deployment permissions; model refusal or a configured permission declaration alone cannot establish denial. Include an authorized control supplying the synthetic detail to B through the broker to verify the detector and permitted access path. Absence of a detail in generated prose alone cannot prove isolation.
